name: apply_global_action
description: Apply a workflow global action to one or more Pimcore elements (max 5 per call). View permission (user + workspace) is enforced per element before the action is applied. Elements are processed independently; per-element outcomes include success + confirmed action, or a stable `error` code (element_not_found, permission_denied, bad_element_entry, service_error).

elements.description: Elements to act on (1..5). Each item: { "id": integer, "type": "asset"|"document"|"data-object" }.

note.description: Optional workflow note (stored as the standard workflow comment).

additionalData.description: Optional additional data forwarded as workflowOptions custom fields.

name: apply_transition
description: Apply a workflow transition to one or more Pimcore elements (max 5 per call). View permission (user + workspace) is enforced per element before the transition is applied. Elements are processed independently; per-element outcomes include success + confirmed action, or a stable `error` code (element_not_found, permission_denied, transition_not_allowed, bad_element_entry, service_error).

elements.description: Elements to transition (1..5). Each item: { "id": integer, "type": "asset"|"document"|"data-object" }.

note.description: Optional workflow note (stored as the standard workflow comment).

additionalData.description: Optional additional data forwarded as workflowOptions custom fields.

name: assign_tag
description: Assign an existing tag to an element (data object, asset, or document). Use list_tags to find tag IDs.

name: create_data_object
description: Create a new data object. Returns the new object ID. Use get_class_definition first to learn required fields. After creation, use update_data_object to set field values.

key.description: Object key (filename). Must be unique within the parent folder. Use lowercase with hyphens (e.g. "my-new-car").

classId.description: Class ID (not name). Get this from list_classes or get_class_definition.

parentId.description: Parent folder ID where the object will be created. Defaults to 1 (root folder).

published.description: Whether to publish the object immediately. Default is false (unpublished). Publish later via update_data_object once all required fields are set.

name: create_document
description: Create a new EMPTY document (Page, Snippet, Email, Link, Hardlink, or Folder). Returns the new document id. See the document-editing skill for the create flow — in particular, always call list_document_types first and pass `docTypeId` for Page/Snippet/Email (without it the document falls back to a stub template and editables render blank).

key.description: Document key (URL slug / filename). Lowercase with hyphens (e.g. "my-new-page"). Must be unique within the parent.

parentId.description: Parent document id (typically a folder). Use search_documents or get_document to find a suitable parent.

type.description: Document type. "page"/"snippet"/"email" have editables; "folder" organizes others; "link"/"hardlink" point elsewhere.

title.description: Page title (used as document title for SEO and navigation; only meaningful for type=page). Empty string by default.

navigationName.description: Navigation name (only meaningful for type=page; stored as a property).

template.description: Twig template (e.g. "content/default.html.twig"). Used when type=page/snippet/email. Leave empty when using docTypeId (the preset supplies the template).

docTypeId.description: docTypeId — id of a preset Document Type. When set, supplies controller+template from the preset. Mutually exclusive with explicit template/controller.

published.description: Whether to publish immediately. Default false — recommended to leave unpublished until populated, then publish via update_document.

name: create_tag
description: Create a new tag. Returns the new tag ID. After creating, use assign_tag to apply it to elements.

parentId.description: Parent tag ID. Use 0 for a root-level tag.

name: describe_tool
description: Get the full parameter schema for a Pimcore tool. Returns parameter names, types, descriptions, and constraints. Use discover first to find tool names.

name: discover
description: Discover available Pimcore tool groups and tools. Call without parameters to list groups. Pass a group name to list tools in that group. Pass a query to search across all groups.

group.description: Group name to list its tools. Omit to list all available groups.

query.description: Keyword to search tools by name/description across all allowed groups.

name: execute
description: Execute a Pimcore tool by name with an arguments object.

name: finalize_task
description: End the current task with a final result. You MUST call this exactly once to complete your task.

name: get_area_brick
description: Return the full schema (editables[], branches[], usageHint, examples[]) for ONE OR MORE Pimcore areabricks in a single call. Pass a comma-separated list of brick ids to fetch every brick you plan to use up-front — each extra round-trip costs the same context replay as a fresh tool call. Discover available brick ids via get_document_schema (`editables[].availableBricks` lists the bricks allowed in each areablock). Returns: {results: [{id, …schema}, …], errors: [{id, error}, …]} — failures on one brick id do not abort the others. See `document-editing` skill for the workflow.

brickIds.description: Areabrick id, OR a comma-separated list of brick ids (e.g. "featurette,product-teaser,text-accordion"). Max

name: get_asset
description: Get a single asset by ID with its metadata. Returns filename, type, path, file size, dimensions (images), and custom metadata. Use format="edit" to get metadata in the normalized format needed by propose_asset_metadata_update, with dataFormatHint per entry showing the expected data structure. Set includeContent to true for thumbnails or text previews.

format.description: Output format: "edit" for normalized metadata with dataFormatHint (use before propose_asset_metadata_update), "preview" (default) for raw metadata.

includeContent.description: When true, includes asset content: a thumbnail image for images/videos, extracted text for PDF/office documents, or a text preview for CSV/JSON/XML files.

previewBytes.description: Maximum bytes to include for text file preview (default 50000). Only applies to text-based assets like CSV, JSON, XML.

name: get_asset_queryable_fields
description: Get all queryable fields for assets. Returns PQL-ready field names, index paths, and types. Use this before writing PQL filters for asset searches.

name: get_class_definition
description: Get the field schema for a data object class. Default returns just {name, type} per field — enough to pick fields for get_data_object(fields=[…]) or to construct a write payload for simple types. For localized fields the children listing is preserved as today. Pass justFieldNames=false to get titles, editableDataFormat hints, examples and metadata. For complex fields (objectbricks, fieldcollections, classificationstore, block), use get_field_schema to explore sub-fields, allowed types, groups, and keys.

className.description: Class name (e.g. "Car", "Customer"). Use list_classes to discover available class names.

justFieldNames.description: When true (default), return only {name, type} per field (localized fields keep their children listing). When false, include title, editableDataFormat hints, examples, and metadata — useful when you need labels or write-format hints.

name: get_data_object
description: Get one or more data objects by ID. Default format is "preview" (compact, all languages of localized fields). Use format="edit" for the structured shape needed by propose_data_object_update. Pass fields=["name","price"] (plain names, NOT PQL paths or locale suffixes) to narrow the response. Pass languages=["en","de"] to limit localized blocks to specific locales. Use search_data_objects first to find object IDs.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Data object IDs. Example: [42, 55, 101]. A JSON-encoded string like "[42, 55, 101]" is also accepted.

format.description: Output format: "preview" (default, compact summaries) or "edit" (structured setter-compatible data for propose_data_object_update).

fields.description: Optional. Plain field names to include, e.g. ["name","price"]. A name matches a top-level field AND any same-named child of localizedFields (one name returns every locale). Use names exactly as in get_class_definition — NOT PQL paths from get_queryable_fields (e.g. "localizedfields.en.name") and NOT locale suffixes (e.g. "name.en"); those decorated forms are coerced when unambiguous, otherwise reported in unknownFields with the valid names. Default: all fields.

languages.description: Optional. Restrict every localizedFields block to just these locales (e.g. ["en","de"]). Default: all valid languages.

name: get_document
description: Get one or more Pimcore documents. By default returns only the document spine (id, type, key, path, parentId, modificationDate, published) — opt in to `includeContent`, `includeSettings`, and `includeProperties` selectively to keep responses small. For SCHEMA (what edits are possible) use get_document_schema; this tool returns CURRENT state. Pass `targetGroupId` to read content for one personalization target group. See the document-editing skill for response shape, when to opt in, and the target-group workflow.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Document IDs. Example: [12, 18]. Max 5 per call — document content can be large; batch conservatively. A JSON-encoded string like "[12, 18]" is also accepted.

includeContent.description: Include the document content (the editable widgets and their current values, areablock entries, blocks, inline-resolved element references). Default false. Opt in when reading or editing content; skip when you only need the spine.

includeSettings.description: Include document settings (title, description, controller, template, prettyUrl). Default false. Opt in when changing those.

includeProperties.description: Include document properties. Default false. Opt in when reading or editing properties.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, content is returned for that target group context (existing variants surfaced; missing ones fall back to base with `inherited: true`). Implies `includeContent: true`.

name: get_document_schema
description: Return the editable schema of one Pimcore document: editables[], structural[] (areablocks/blocks with availableBricks palette), branches[]. See `document-editing` skill for naming conventions, write payload shapes, and per-type examples.

name: get_element_tags
description: Get all tags assigned to a specific element (data object, asset, or document). Returns tag IDs, names, and paths.

name: get_element_workflow_details
description: Get the current state, allowed transitions, and global actions for an element in each applicable workflow. Pass workflowName to filter to a single workflow. The graph SVG is omitted — use get_workflow_graph if you need it.

workflowName.description: Optional. Filter to a single workflow by name. Empty string = return all applicable workflows.

name: get_field_schema
description: Get detailed schema for a specific field in a data object class. Use dot notation to drill into complex fields: "localizedfields" for localized sub-fields, "attributes.Engine" for a specific objectbrick, "content.NewsCars" for a specific fieldcollection type. For classification stores, use groupId to get keys for a specific group.

groupId.description: For classification store fields: get keys for this group ID.

name: get_queryable_fields
description: Get all queryable fields for a data object class. Returns each field as {pqlField, type}; pqlField is what the search tool consumes. Use this before writing PQL filters to discover available fields. These pqlField names are for pqlFilter ONLY — to read values with get_data_object, use plain field names from get_class_definition, not these dotted paths.

name: get_workflow_graph
description: Render a workflow diagram for a specific element as SVG. Returns the raw SVG string.

name: get_workflow_places
description: List every place (state) configured for a Pimcore workflow, including label, color, and header-visibility flag. Per-element layout id is exposed by get_element_workflow_details, not this tool (layout resolution requires element context).

name: list_agent_templates
description: List agent-generated Twig templates visible to the current user. Non-admin users see only their own active templates; admins see all active templates. Returns { templates: [{slug, label, type, status, updatedAt}] }.

name: list_assets
description: Browse assets in a folder. Returns asset IDs, filenames, types, paths, and file sizes. Use parentId=1 (root) to start browsing.

parentId.description: Parent folder ID to list. Default: 1 (root folder).

name: list_classes
description: List all available Pimcore data object classes. Returns class names, IDs, and field summaries. Use this first to discover what data types exist before searching.

name: list_document_types
description: List the Pimcore Document Types (presets) configured for this project. Each preset bundles a controller + template so newly-created pages render real content from the start.

name: list_editables
description: Return the sorted list of Pimcore document editable type names available in this project (e.g. input, textarea, wysiwyg, image, link, areablock, block, select, …). Call this before generating a Twig template so you know which pimcore_* Twig functions are safe to use. Returns: { editableTypes: string[] }.

name: list_elements_by_workflow_state
description: List Pimcore elements filtered by workflow name and (optionally) current place. Paged; pageSize is clamped to 100.

stateName.description: Optional. Filter by current place/state name. Empty = return elements in any state.

pageSize.description: Page size (1..100). Values >100 are clamped to 100.

name: list_tags
description: List available tags. Optionally filter by parent tag to browse the tag hierarchy. Returns tag IDs, names, paths, and parent IDs.

parentId.description: Parent tag ID to list children of. Omit or set to 0 to list root-level tags.

timeoutMs.description: Soft wall-clock budget in milliseconds. Default: 5000. If listing the subtree takes longer, the result includes a recovery hint suggesting how to narrow the request and retry.

name: list_target_groups
description: List active Pimcore personalization target groups (used to author target-group-specific document variants). Returns `{available: bool, targetGroups: [{id, name}]}`. When the personalization-bundle is not installed, returns `{available: false, targetGroups: []}` — in that case do not pass `targetGroupId` to get_document, propose_document_update, or update_document; those calls will fail.

name: list_thumbnail_configs
description: List the project's named thumbnail configurations of the given type, with target dimensions. Pass type="image" or type="video". Use a returned `name` as the `thumbnail` option of pimcore_image / pimcore_video. For pimcore_video a named config is REQUIRED — an inline array fatals at edit time. Each entry: { name, mode, width, height, group?, description? }. `width`/`height` may be null, meaning that axis scales to the source asset's aspect ratio (e.g. scaleByWidth); a fixed-box mode (cover/resize) gives an exact slot size. Returns { thumbnails: [...] }.

type.description: Which kind of thumbnail configs to list: "image" or "video".

name: list_workflows
description: List configured Pimcore workflows. With no parameters returns every workflow name. Pass elementId + elementType to filter to workflows applicable to that element (returns name and label for each).

elementId.description: Optional Pimcore element ID. Must be given together with elementType.

elementType.description: Optional element type: "asset" | "document" | "data-object". Must be given together with elementId.

name: propose_agent_template
description: Propose a new or updated Twig template for user approval. Validates the template and runs a sandboxed test-render; if both pass, stores the payload server-side and returns a proposalId. Nothing is written to disk until a human approves the proposal in Studio. Use action=create for new templates, action=update to replace an existing one. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once the proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. contextDocumentId (optional, integer) — when set, the proposal widget links to this document via Open / Refresh buttons and the resolver re-checks it at approve time. reassignDocument (optional, boolean) — when true (with contextDocumentId), the resolver also reassigns the document's template field to this slug on approve. Use for clone-and-reassign refinement of a non-agent template.

action.description: Operation: "create" for a new template, "update" to replace an existing one.

slug.description: Unique slug identifier for the template (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores).

label.description: Human-readable label shown in the Studio template dropdown.

main.description: Complete Twig source for the template file.

description.description: Optional description of the template's purpose.

contextDocumentId.description: Optional document this proposal is about. The widget will offer "Open document" / refresh on approve. For update: doc.template MUST already equal the proposed slug. For create without reassign: same. For create WITH reassignDocument=true: doc.template MUST NOT equal the slug (clone-and-reassign path). Rejected for partial templates.

reassignDocument.description: When true (and contextDocumentId is set), on approve the resolver also setTemplate() on the doc to point at this slug. Used for clone-and-reassign refinement when the doc was on a project (non-agent) template. Defaults to false.

name: propose_agent_template_deletion
description: Propose the deletion of an existing agent-generated Twig template. Resolves which documents are bound to the template and which other templates include it, then stores a deletion proposal for human review. Nothing is deleted until a human approves the proposal in Studio. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once the proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

slug.description: Unique slug identifier of the template to delete.

name: propose_asset_metadata_update
description: Propose custom metadata changes to one or more assets for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals — pass it directly, never as a string. Each entry: {"id": <assetId>, "metadata": [{name, language, type, data}, ...]}. Use get_asset with format="edit" first to see the exact names, types, and dataFormatHint per metadata entry — copy them verbatim. IMPORTANT: `data` values are LITERAL JSON. For relations write {"id": <int>, "type": "object"|"asset"|"document"} as a literal object, never a JSON-encoded string. Multi-relation fields (type "manyToManyRelation") are ADDITIVE by default: send only the member(s) you want to add and existing relations are preserved (de-duplicated by id+type). To overwrite the whole list instead, set "replace": true on that metadata entry. Example (placeholders in <angle brackets>): [{"id": 42, "metadata": [{"name": "<metadataName>", "language": "", "type": "input", "data": "<literal string value>"}, {"name": "<relationMetadataName>", "language": "", "type": "object", "data": {"id": 7, "type": "object"}}]}].

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

name: propose_data_object_update
description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

name: propose_document_update
description: Propose changes to one or more Pimcore documents for user approval. Does NOT write — stores the validated payload server-side and returns a proposalId per document; the user reviews each proposal in a chat-side modal and approves or rejects. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. Use for non-trivial / visible / multi-section changes; use update_document for small explicitly-authorized edits. See the document-editing skill for editable naming, areablock/block composition, and target-group (personalization) rules — all required reading before calling.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <documentId>, "data": {<update_document data>}, "targetGroupId": <int, optional>}. The "data" shape is identical to update_document's data argument: {"editables": {...}, "settings": {...}, "properties": {...}, "appendEditables": <bool>}. When "targetGroupId" is set, only "editables" is allowed in "data". Max 20 entries per call. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the array is re-stringified.

id.description: Single-document shortcut: document id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE document — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, editables?, settings?, properties?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-document shortcut: full data envelope ({editables?, settings?, properties?, appendEditables?}).

targetGroupId.description: Single-document shortcut: personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty. Applies ONLY to the single-document shortcut (paired with `id`). Ignored when `proposals` is provided — use per-entry `targetGroupId` in that case.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

name: propose_tag_assignment
description: Propose tag changes for one or more elements for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. tagIds is the complete desired set — include existing tags to keep, omit tags to remove.

proposals.description: Array of tag proposals — pass it directly, never as a string. Each entry: {"elementType": "object"|"asset"|"document", "elementId": <id>, "tagIds": [<tagId>, ...]}. IMPORTANT: `tagIds` is the COMPLETE desired set of tags for the element, NOT a delta. Include existing tags you want to keep, omit tags you want to remove. Use get_element_tags first to read the current set. Tag IDs are LITERAL integers in a literal array — never wrap them in a JSON-encoded string. Example: [{"elementType": "object", "elementId": 42, "tagIds": [1, 5, 12]}].

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

name: search_assets
description: Search assets: identifier/filename token search + PQL filter, parent folder scope, pagination. There is no separate list_assets tool — to list a known folder's assets, pass parentId. Returns id, filename, type, path. Before using pqlFilter, call skill("pql-search") once per turn.

query.description: Identifier/filename token search. Matches identifier and filename tokens, NOT human-readable metadata. To list a known folder's assets pass parentId; to match a filename pattern or metadata field use pqlFilter.

pqlFilter.description: PQL filter for assets. Common fields: id, type, filename, fullPath. LIKE wildcards are `*` and `?` — NOT SQL `%` / `_`. Examples: type = "image"; filename LIKE "*.pdf"; fullPath LIKE "/<FolderName>/*"

parentId.description: Parent folder ID to scope the search. Omit for global search.

name: search_data_objects
description: Search data objects: fulltext + PQL filter, class filter, pagination. By default returns only ids per hit (use them with get_data_object). Pass extended=true to also get key, className, path, published, modificationDate. Before using pqlFilter, call skill("pql-search") once per turn.

query.description: Fulltext search term (searches across all indexed fields). Leave empty to list all objects of a class.

className.description: Filter by class name (selects the class, e.g. "<ClassName>"). NOTE: className selects the class, not a field value — to filter by a field value (including objectType) use pqlFilter instead. Strongly recommended for focused results.

pqlFilter.description: PQL filter — use this to filter by any field value (including objectType); NOT raw SQL. Call get_queryable_fields first for field names/types. LIKE wildcards are `*` and `?` — NOT SQL `%` / `_`. Example: fieldName = "value" AND year > 2000

parentId.description: Parent folder ID to scope the search. Omit for global search.

extended.description: When true, each hit includes key, className, path, published, modificationDate in addition to id. Default false (ids only) — fetch details via get_data_object.

name: search_documents
description: Search Pimcore documents: fulltext + PQL filter, parent folder scope, pagination. Returns id, key, type, path, published. Filter by document type (page/snippet/email/link/hardlink/folder) via PQL: type = "page". Before using pqlFilter, call skill("pql-search") once per turn.

query.description: Fulltext search term. Searches document key/title/path.

pqlFilter.description: PQL filter for documents. Common fields: id, type, key, fullPath, published. LIKE wildcards are `*` and `?` — NOT SQL `%` / `_`. Examples: type = "page"; key LIKE "*home*"; published = true

parentId.description: Parent folder ID to scope the search. Omit for global search.

excludeFolders.description: Exclude folder documents from results. Default: false.

name: stage_asset
description: Stage a Pimcore asset to the local filesystem for analysis. Returns a local file path that can be used with read_file and grep to inspect the file content. Use this for large files (CSV, XML, JSON) that need detailed analysis beyond the preview from get_asset.

id.description: The Pimcore asset ID to stage.

name: stage_file_set
description: Copy a developer-curated set of project files to this chat session's workspace so you can read them with view/grep/glob. Returns the local paths of the staged files. Call again at any time to refresh (full re-copy).

name: unassign_tag
description: Remove a tag from an element (data object, asset, or document). Use get_element_tags to see current tags.

name: update_asset
description: Update an asset's key or custom metadata fields. Does not replace binary content. Pass field updates as an object of field/value pairs.

data.description: Fields to update, as an object of field/value pairs — pass it directly, never as a string. Supported: "key" (rename), custom metadata fields. Example: {"key": "new-filename.jpg"}

name: update_data_object
description: Update field values on an existing data object. Pass a JSON object mapping field names to new values. Use get_class_definition to learn field names and types.

id.description: The data object ID to update.

data.description: JSON object of field values to set. Example: {"name": "Red Car", "color": "red", "price": 25000}. Only include fields you want to change.

name: update_document
description: Update editables, settings, and/or properties on an existing document. Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). Partial updates preserve other editables (appendEditables defaults to true). Pre-flights validation; on validation failure no save happens. After successful save, post-renders the document and returns any frontend errors in `renderErrors[]` — if non-empty, the document was saved BUT renders broken; pick different element ids/values and call update_document again to fix.For schema and current state, call get_document_schema and get_document first.

data.description: Object with optional keys: editables, settings, properties, appendEditables. Example: {"editables": {"headline": "New title", "cImage_3": {"id": 341}}, "settings": {"published": true}, "properties": {"navigation_color": {"type": "text", "data": "blue"}}}. Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

name: upload_asset
description: Upload a new asset from base64-encoded content. Creates the asset in the specified parent folder.

parentId.description: Parent folder ID for the new asset.
